hook: Skipping your 401 k match is like turning down a raise.

blocks.narration: Skipping your 401 k match is like turning down a raise. And a lot of people do it every single year.
blocks.visual: A clay office worker pushes away a glowing envelope across a desk, coworkers blurred in the background

blocks.narration: Many American employers match part of what you save for retirement. You put money in, and your company adds extra on top.
blocks.visual: Two clay hands drop coins into the same jar, one from the worker and one from a company building

blocks.narration: A common formula is fifty percent of your contributions, up to six percent of your salary. Here is what that actually means.
blocks.visual: Clay number tiles fifty and six slide into place on a simple balance scale

blocks.narration: On a sixty thousand dollar salary, saving six percent means three thousand six hundred dollars a year from your paycheck.
blocks.visual: A paycheck shaped like a flag slides out of a clay printer, a slice of it flowing into a jar

blocks.narration: Your employer then adds half of that, which is one thousand eight hundred dollars a year you did not have to earn.
blocks.visual: A second smaller stream of coins pours into the jar from above, glowing brighter

blocks.narration: That is an instant fifty percent return on that money, before any investment growth even begins. Nothing else reliably does that.
blocks.visual: A gauge needle swings up to a bright green zone as the jar fills

blocks.narration: Some plans have vesting schedules, meaning you must stay a certain time to keep the match. Check your benefits portal for the rules.
blocks.visual: A clay clock on the wall ticks while a little lock on the jar slowly opens

blocks.narration: Contribute at least enough to get the full match if you can. Share this with a coworker who has not signed up yet.
blocks.visual: The worker now pulls the glowing envelope close and smiles, confetti drifting down

cta: Share this with a coworker who has not signed up yet.

captions.hook_line: Not taking your 401(k) match is like turning down a raise 💸
captions.body: If your employer matches 50% of contributions up to 6% of pay, saving 6% of a $60,000 salary adds $1,800 a year from your employer. Check your plan's exact formula.

youtube_title: Your 401(k) Match Is a Raise You're Skipping
